Sample Name: Followup for Coronary Artery Disease and Episodic Symptoms
Description: Followup following cardiac treatment and rehabilitation with intermittent brief head pain and exertional dyspnea.
HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS: The patient presents with several concerns during followup for significant coronary artery disease and recent cardiac care. He experiences rare, sudden, very severe pains in the left temporal region that last only briefly. He also reports shortness of breath after walking a short distance outdoors or climbing stairs, although he tolerates approximately 20 minutes of supervised exercise during cardiac rehabilitation. Previous recent cardiac testing and performance in rehabilitation have been reassuring. He raises concerns about past exposures, a toe problem, sexual function, and medication effects. Difficulty achieving or maintaining an erection was discussed in the context of cardiovascular disease, medication use including venlafaxine, and anxiety. There is no confirmed cause for these symptoms in this encounter.
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION: Blood pressure and pulse were satisfactory. Examination included the affected toe and cardiopulmonary assessment. No new acute cardiopulmonary finding was described.
IMPRESSION AND PLAN:
1. Coronary artery disease, status post recent treatment. Continue prescribed cardiovascular medication, lipid control, diet and structured exercise. Recent studies and rehabilitation progress were reviewed as reassuring.
2. Intermittent exertional dyspnea. Continue monitoring. Symptoms may be influenced by abrupt exertion outside rehabilitation; reassess if worsening or persistent.
3. Brief, infrequent temporal head pains. Observe for a change in frequency, duration, severity, or associated symptoms and contact the clinic if they progress.
4. Erectile dysfunction, potentially multifactorial. Discussed cardiovascular risk, anxiety, and possible medication effects. Continue current management and reassess before considering changes to psychiatric medication.
5. Preventive care. Reviewed colonoscopy and immunization history. One-time HIV screening was offered for the next laboratory visit.
Followup in six months, with routine laboratory work and earlier reassessment for worsening symptoms.
